title: VMAFx run-result timeline, schema version 1
description: One versioned report format for a scoring run's provenance, per-frame scores, per-window statistics and events (vidiko/vmafx#2452, RC5). Every object this schema owns is closed (additionalProperties false), with three pass-through exceptions whose field contracts live elsewhere: provenance is the record of vmafx_context_provenance_json() (RC4 WP5, #2288; the authoritative field contract is the OpenAPI Provenance schema in api/openapi/vmafx-server-v1.yaml and the VmafxProvenance definition in core/api/vmafx.toml), scoring_configuration is the option surface of #2258 (the ScoreOptions component of the same OpenAPI document), and an event's detail object is writer-defined. Those three stay open, so a field added by their single source does not take a timeline-schema version. The scores object is a different exception: it is a dynamic feature-name map, not a closed object with fixed members, so a new feature name does not take a version. The event vocabulary is fixed, so a change that adds an event type takes a new schema version and a version-1 reader refuses a document it does not know by name; newer versions are additive supersets (never removed, renamed or retyped). The versioning model is ADR-3538. docs/api/run-result-timeline.md is the human reference. The skeleton pins the four sections' identities, not yet their full field contracts. A window's start and end must use the same time-key kind and start must strictly precede end; a frame or event series must use one common set of time-key kinds and compare strictly (frames) or non-decreasingly (events). JSON Schema cannot compare time keys, so api/run_result_timeline_contract.py enforces those rules together with the OpenAPI sections. A time key carrying more than one coordinate kind must have all of them describe the same instant. The C ABI writer/reader and the byte-equal write-read-write identity check land in the follow-up PRs of the same issue.

schema_version.description: The schema version the document was written against. 1 is the shape this file defines; a reader refuses an unknown version by name (#2452 acceptance).

frames.description: The per-frame series, in strictly ascending time-key order: one entry per scored frame, each with a non-empty feature-score map. The semantic validator orders entries by the first common coordinate (frame_index, then timestamp_ns, then timecode) and rejects duplicate or out-of-order keys.

windows.description: Per-window statistics over ranges of the timeline: pooling and aggregation results.

events.description: The run's events, in non-decreasing time-key order, ordered by the first common coordinate (frame_index, then timestamp_ns, then timecode): alignment decisions, drops, repeats, freezes, switches and masked areas. The semantic validator rejects out-of-order event keys.

time_key.description: Where an entry sits on the timeline: at least one of the 0-based frame index, the presentation timestamp in nanoseconds from the run's zero, or the SMPTE-style timecode. A writer carries what the run knows - a frame score carries the frame index, a wall-clock event carries the timestamp - and an empty time key is refused. A frame or event series is ordered by the first coordinate every entry carries, in the fixed priority frame_index, timestamp_ns, timecode; this makes a series with mixed optional coordinates sortable. When an entry carries more than one kind they must describe the same instant. Timecode comparison is by its HH:MM:SS[:FF] fields, not by a frame-rate-dependent drop-frame count.

frame_index.description: 0-based display order, the stream-metadata display_index of api/stream-metadata-fields.json.

timestamp_ns.description: Presentation timestamp in nanoseconds from the run's zero.

timecode.description: SMPTE-style HH:MM:SS or HH:MM:SS:FF timecode, optionally drop-frame with a semicolon before the frames. Hours, minutes and seconds are bounded; the frames field depends on the frame rate, so the reader checks it.

provenance.description: The provenance record of the context that produced the run: vmafx_context_provenance_json() (RC4 WP5, #2288) carries one key per field of VmafxProvenance and its models, features and annotations. The authoritative field contract is the OpenAPI Provenance schema (api/openapi/vmafx-server-v1.yaml) and the VmafxProvenance definition in core/api/vmafx.toml; this schema pins the identity anchor so a timeline stays attributable and leaves the field contract to that single source.

digest.description: The record's own digest: the digest member of VmafxProvenance, the SHA-256 of the record's canonical JSON (RFC 8785) without digest and elapsed_ns.

scoring_configuration.description: The scoring-option surface in effect for the run (#2258, WP8): the ScoreOptions component of the scoring group in api/openapi/vmafx-server-v1.yaml. The skeleton leaves the members to that single source; a timeline-only JSON-Schema validator therefore accepts any object here. Callers validate this section through api/run_result_timeline_contract.py, which applies the ScoreOptions contract too.

frame_score.description: One scored frame: its time key and the non-empty map of scores written for it.

scores.description: Dynamic feature-name map: keys are feature names as the mounted models name them (for example vmaf, integer_adm2); values are that frame's numbers for the feature, null for a non-finite result as the CLI's JSON output writes it (core/src/output.cpp, json_write_frame_metric). A frame must carry at least one score; a new feature name does not take a schema version because the keys are not schema-owned members.

window_statistic.description: One statistic computed over a window of the timeline. The start and end must share a sortable time-key coordinate and start must strictly precede end; JSON Schema cannot compare time keys, so api/run_result_timeline_contract.py enforces that rule. When both ends are frame indices the interval is half-open (start inclusive, end exclusive).

statistic.description: The statistic's name as the writer computes it (for example pooled, mean, worst_frame).

feature.description: The feature the statistic belongs to; omitted for a run-level statistic.

value.description: The computed value as a JSON number; null for a non-finite result, as the CLI's JSON output writes it (core/src/output.cpp, json_write_frame_metric).

event.description: One run event. A planted event without a time key is refused by name (#2452 acceptance).

type.description: alignment_decision records how streams were aligned; drop, repeat and freeze record frame-handling decisions; switch records a source or configuration switch mid-run; masked_area records a region excluded from scoring. The vocabulary grows additively under HISS-14.

detail.description: The event's facts as the writer reports them (for example the alignment offsets of an alignment_decision); the skeleton constrains nothing further.
